notes.decision: Translated 'their (hearts/lips)' tentatively. The form ϩⲧⲏⲩ is unusual; in context (placing X to speak the truth in one heart) it must denote a faculty of speech or seat of intention. Possibly Lyc plural of ϩⲏⲧ 'heart' or related to a body-part for speaking. The transcription [2] follows the page's convention where 2 = ϩ; here the bracket marks the ϩ as editorially restored.
Translated 'which is divided' from ⲡⲱⲣⲭ/ⲡⲱⲣϫ 'separate, divide' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ). Sense uncertain in this fragmentary line.

Marginal Coptic numeral 'ⲟⲏ' = 78. This is the chapter number for Kephalaion 78 (the new chapter beginning at line 12). Preserved as numerical paratext; the second instance 'ⲟⲏ ⲟⲏ' between lines 12-13 is similar marginalia, omitted from the line array as it bears no line number.

ⲡⲩⲧⲁⲩ = 'the four' (Lyc, in glossary); ⲛϩⲱⲃ = 'of works/matters.' The chapter title 'Concerning the Four Matters on account of which men kill one another for them' enumerates four worldly preoccupations — food (line 17-18), sexual intercourse (lines 19-21), wealth (lines 21-23), and war/violence (lines 24-27).

Translated 'the care of the mouth' — i.e., the bodily concern for eating that drives men to violence. ⲡⲣⲁⲩϣ (editor's tentative restoration with ?) = 'care, anxiety, preoccupation' (cf. Sah. ⲣⲟⲟⲩϣ); ⲡⲣⲱ = 'the mouth,' here metonymic for nourishment. Confirmed by ⲭⲉ ⲉⲩⲛⲁⲟⲩⲱⲙ 'that they shall eat' which follows.

Translated 'joining themselves into it.' The form ⲃⲉⲗⲏ is obscure; possibly related to ⲡⲱⲗ 'be loosed/dissolve' (giving 'dissolving themselves in it') or to a verb of mingling. ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'in it (fem.)' refers back to ⲡⲟⲣⲛⲓⲁ. Captures the sexual intermingling sense fitting the second of the four works.

Translated 'frenzy' (line 24 ⲛⲗⲉⲃ- + line 25 -ⲉ giving ⲛⲗⲉⲃⲉ). Likely Lyc form of ⲗⲓⲃⲉ 'madness, fury' (Sah). Forms part of the war-vice catalogue with ⲡⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ 'war,' ⲫⲓⲗⲟⲛⲓⲕⲓⲁ 'contention,' and ⲛⲁⲓⲕⲏ (= ἀδικίαι 'injustices').
Greek loanword ἀδικίαι 'injustices' with characteristic Lyc reduction ⲁⲇⲓ → ⲁⲓ. Part of the standard moral-vice catalogue.

Translated 'they may take a name' — Coptic idiom for acquiring fame/reputation. ⲁⲩⲭⲓ = ⲁⲩϫⲓ 'they take' (Lyc ⲭ for ϫ); ⲟⲩⲣⲉⲛ = 'a name.' This concludes the war-vices section: men kill in tyranny to make a name for themselves.

Translated 'tongues' (= peoples, languages). Lyc plural of ⲁⲥⲡⲉ 'tongue, language' (Sah). The phrase ϩⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ⲉⲥⲡⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'in/among all the tongues' = 'among all peoples,' fitting the universal scope of the four works.

Translated 'they slaughter (one another)' — from ⲥⲱⲭⲉ 'slaughter, smite' (in glossary as 'slaughter/wounding'). Fits the chapter theme: men in all peoples slaughter one another that they may obtain the four works.

Parsed as ⲭⲉ ⲉⲩⲁ-ⲭⲡ-ⲧⲁⲩ ⲛⲉⲩ = 'in order that they may take/seize them for themselves.' ⲭⲡ likely Lyc form of ϣⲱⲡ 'receive' or ϫⲡⲟ 'acquire'; ⲧⲁⲩ = 3pl object 'them' (referring to the four works). The clause expresses purpose.
